jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Hayward Onsite/Exempt

Salary:
$160,000 - $180,000 + Benefits

CRIL History and Independent Living Philosophy

Community Resources for Independent Living (CRIL) was organized in 1979. CRIL’s main office is located in Hayward with branch offices in Fremont and Livermore. CRIL is a part of a statewide and national network of 28 Independent Living Centers (ILCs) in California and over 400 in the US. In 1972, the first ILC was formed in Berkeley, CA by Ed Roberts, who became the first student with a significant disability to enroll, along with other college students at UC Berkeley. This sparked the independent living (IL) revolution that changed national law. Independent Living (IL) is a philosophy grounded in the principle that people with disabilities are the experts on their own lives. It champions the right of people with disabilities to make personal decisions, direct their own services, participate fully in community life, and empowers people to live as independently as they choose.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to provide executive leadership to a disability-led organization advancing disability rights, systemic change, and equity for people living with disabilities and seniors throughout southern and eastern Alameda County. CRIL’s main office is in Hayward with additional sites in Fremont and Livermore. CRIL currently has an Operating Budget of $2.2 ML, 20 employees, and 7 board members. CRIL thrives on a peer-based model where the staff and board reflect and understand the communities they serve.

Summary

As Executive Director, you will provide overall leadership and direction for CRIL and will be responsible for advancing the organization’s mission and strategy. Reporting to the Board of Directors, you will oversee the day-to-day operations, strategic planning, and staff management for CRIL. This includes managing 6 direct reports. This role ensures the agency fulfills its mission of supporting people with disabilities through advocacy, services, and community partnerships.
Strategic Leadership(15%)

Develop and champion the organizational advocacy agenda; ensure all systems-change efforts align with CRIL’s mission and strategic priorities to advance disability rights public policy at the local, state, and federal levels.
Educate policymakers on emerging issues and independent living (IL) priorities of people with disabilities.
Support and resource the System Change Advocate and Community Organizer in building relationships with civic leaders, public agencies, and community organizations to advance systems change.
Empower consumers and community advocates in their self-advocacy and collective efforts.
Lead advocacy for disability rights at executive-level forums, including active participation alongside the Systems Change Advocate and Community Organizer in Alameda County’s Aging and Disability Resource Connection (ADRC). CRIL serves as the fiscal agent for the Alameda County ADRC.

Community Engagement (20%)

Represent CRIL in the community; build and maintain partnerships with disability advocacy coalitions, other agencies, and local government entities.
Strengthen CRIL’s relationships with consumers and disability advocates throughout its service area.
Communicate CRIL’s mission, programs, advocacy priorities, and community impact to a wide range of audiences.

Fundraising & Development (20%)

Lead fund development and strategic planning with the Board of Directors & appropriate staff.
Oversee grants, donor engagement, financial reporting, and funder relationships.
Work with the Board to develop and implement a 3-year Strategic Plan and an annual fund development plan, including government grants and contracts, foundation support, individual giving, and other sources of revenue.

Programs & Evaluation (15%)

Monitor program delivery and align services with community needs and CRIL’s mission.
Oversee the quality, accessibility, regulatory compliance, and outcomes of CRIL’s programs across all service locations.
Use consumer feedback and program data to identify needs, improve services, and inform systems-change priorities.

Administration & Staff Development (15%)

Guide staff team and the organization through transitions such as leadership changes and structural shifts.
Negotiate all agency contracts and ensure contract compliance.
Partner with the Human Resources Coordinator to recruit, hire, support, and retain a skilled, diverse staff, with a broad range of skills consistent with the community CRIL serves.
Oversee professional development and performance evaluations.
Create an annual professional development plan designed to develop staff’s skills.
Ensure compliance with personnel policies established by the Board of Directors and in line with all local, state, and federal labor regulations.
Ensure all job descriptions are up to date and annual performance evaluations are completed.

Financial Management (10%)

Oversee the development and management of the organization’s annual budget, and provide report-outs on budget vs. actuals regularly to the Board.
Ensure fiduciary responsibility and financial accountability for all contributions, income, and agency assets, seeing that all funds are disbursed in accordance with contract requirements and donor designations.
Identify and manage organizational risks by maintaining effective internal controls, policies, and risk-management practices that protect CRIL’s assets, support regulatory and contractual compliance, and promote safe and reliable operations.
Evaluate and create a strategy for funding diversification - federal, state, city, & private.

Board Support and Partnership (5%)

Report regularly to the Board of Directors regarding organizational objectives, financial status of the organization, and other issues relevant to the Board. Ensure transparency and alignment with organizational goals.
Provide the Board of Directors with adequate information to assist members in reaching decisions and in formulating necessary policies.
Assist the Board of Directors in their roles and responsibilities by providing support, education, and leadership development.
Help recruit new Board members that align with the needs of the Board.

Required Qualifications:

CRIL is a disability-led, peer-based organization and seeks a leader whose experience reflects the communities CRIL serves.
Bachelor’s degree required.
5+ years of senior leadership experience in the nonprofit or public sector.
Strong staff and team development experience, including leading diverse teams across different cultures and languages.
Experience overseeing programs or operations across multiple locations.
Proven fundraising and grant writing skills.
Strong financial management skills with $1.5M+ budgets.
Demonstrated ability to build community relationships and communicate effectively with consumers, policymakers, funders, and other partners.
Ability to use contemporary digital tools for communication, reporting, and organizational management with or without accommodations. Ability to work some evenings/weekends and travel occasionally in-state.

Preferred:

Experience with communications, outreach, media relations, or organizational visibility
Knowledge of CRIL’s service areas (Hayward, Fremont, and Livermore).
Bilingual in Spanish, ASL, or other threshold languages.

Comprehensive Benefits Package:

Competitive paid time off including 3 weeks’ vacation and 70 hours of sick leave.
Retirement savings with a 3% match for 403b plans.
Full medical, dental, and vision insurance coverage.

CRIL IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

CRIL is a disability-led, peer-based organization and seeks a leader whose experience reflects the communities CRIL serves. Candidates with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Deep knowledge of the independent living philosophy, disability rights, and consumer-controlled services is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities.

Lead projects, programs or initiatives including but not limited to advocacy efforts, education and professional development, community initiatives, overall membership engagement, and more.
Drive continued P&E Wing growth at the national and Chapter levels, while working closely with the Chief Awards & Global Industry Officer on global and national expansion and with the Chapter and National Member Engagement teams on guiding the 12 Chapter P&E Wing Committees so that they customize their approach for their communities while sharing knowledge, strategy and executable goals.

Work closely with the Chief Advocacy Officer of the Academy on initiatives including connections with key lawmakers on a national level to ensure context and education for key legislative matters, including those related to artificial intelligence and its impact on music creators.
Monitor and interpret emerging technology trends—including AI, machine learning-driven production tools, and immersive/spatial audio formats—and their impact on the producer and engineer communities, translating these trends into member education, White Papers, panels and strategic advocacy positions.
Serve as the P&E Wing's representative in the Academy's broader conversations on responsible AI use in music, including matters of credit, compensation, consent and disclosure, ensuring the perspective of working producers and engineers is reflected in Academy positions.
Curate the P&E Wing Advisory Council and related Committees, working with the P&E Wing Steering Committee Co-Chairs and the Chief Awards & Global Industry Officer.
Oversee the curation of the Special Merit Technical Award on an annual basis, in conjunction with the Technical Grammy Award Committee and its Chair or Co-Chairs
Oversee, secure sponsors for and direct the planning and execution of the annual P&E Wing Grammy Week event, working with P&E Wing staff, internal Academy production, outside vendors, artist relations, legal, partnerships and MarComms teams.
Curate the selection of the annual honoree(s) at the P&E Wing Grammy Week event in conjunction with the P&E Wing Steering Committee, Academy CEO and the Chief Awards & Global Industry Officer.

Qualifications

7+ years of music industry experience, preferably as a working producer or engineer or in direct service to these communities.
Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
Maintains a strong working knowledge of emerging technologies shaping music production and engineering, including AI-assisted and AI-generated production tools, machine learning applications in audio, and immersive/spatial audio formats. Able to evaluate the opportunities and challenges these technologies pose for producers and engineers and translate them into practical guidance, programming and advocacy positions for the community.
Ability to maintain composure in high-stress, complex situations to ensure the smooth and efficient running of an event; has excellent decision-making skills, clear communication and delegation; fosters welcoming hospitality.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail. Keeps information organized and accessible, works efficiently while managing workload. Prioritizes tasks appropriately and manages time well. Adapts well to change, is flexible and open-minded to new ideas, solicits performance feedback and handles constructive criticism, takes on new responsibilities, handles pressure, adjusts plans to meet changing needs.
Communicates well both verbally and in writing, shares information and ideas with others, has good listening skills, builds strong relationships, consistently demonstrates positive and professional demeanor, negotiates effectively.
Contributes to and helps team meet all team deadlines and goals, listens to others and values opinions, welcomes newcomers and promotes a team atmosphere. Meets commitments, stays focused under pressure, and meets attendance/punctuality requirements.

These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com.

Role Overview

As Chief of Staff to the CEO, you will sit at the center of how this company operates and makes decisions. You will own the operating cadence, drive cross-functional initiatives from problem definition to resolution, and handle the work that keeps the CEO focused on the highest-leverage problems. That means being equally comfortable in a budget-versus-actual, a headcount model, or an organizational question that needs someone to push it to closure.

You think clearly under pressure, communicate with precision, and know how to move work forward with the best judgement. You understand how AI tools can accelerate serious work, and you use them that way. If you want a front row seat to how a CEO makes decisions and how a growth-stage company actually scales, this role delivers that.

Who You Are

Strategic Partner to the CEO:

Trusted confidant and advisor to the CEO. Helping think through complex strategic, financial, and personnel decisions, and ensuring they are executed upon.
Ability to disseminate information and communicate ideas on behalf of the CEO to the Executive Leadership Team and external stakeholders.
Track record of “clearing the path”. Taking ownership of day-to-day operations and cross-functional processes to create more leverage for the CEO.
Strong financial and operational judgment: able to read and synthesize P&L data, budget variances, and headcount plans to inform executive-level decision-making with clarity and speed.
Strategic thinker, excellent problem solver, and first-class communicator.
Natural curiosity, particularly around how AI is being adopted across industries and how it drives measurable ROI, and the ability to bring those insights back to inform how OpenGov operates and competes.

Excellent Operator

Ability to lead and drive timely execution of business critical and cross-functional strategic initiatives in a fast-paced environment.
Seamlessly break down large and complex concepts into actionable tasks and steps.
Experience building and maintaining an operating cadence that promotes alignment, accountability, and knowledge-sharing at the executive level.
Ability to synthesize complex, competing information quickly and form an independent point of view — then move work forward decisively, even under pressure and without complete information.

Clear Communicator

Track record of effectively communicating, influencing, and driving alignment across executive leadership and beyond.
High EQ with the ability to identify the needs of OpenGov’s Executive Leadership Team, build strong relationships among internal and external stakeholders, and promote a culture of trust and transparency.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and attention to detail.

Customer Obsessed

Genuine commitment to understanding the needs of OpenGov's customers and ensuring their voice is represented in executive-level decisions and company priorities.
Approaches every cross-functional initiative with a lens of customer impact — not just internal efficiency.

What You'll Do

Own the company-wide operating cadence: company all-hands meetings, Executive Leadership Team meetings, and quarterly offsites. This includes agenda-setting, logistics, notetaking, and follow through on decisions.
Own the company's goal-setting process end to end, from framework design and OKR cycle coordination to tracking progress and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
Drive alignment and accountability across the Executive Leadership Team, ensuring the organization stays focused on the highest-priority challenges and executes with urgency.
Triage and manage competing priorities for the CEO: synthesize complex inputs, frame decision options, and surface key insights to inform executive-level choices.
Conduct ad-hoc financial and operational analyses diagnosing business challenges and recommending tailored, scalable solutions.
Partner with Finance on review cycles and headcount analysis; synthesizing financial data into clear, actionable recommendations for the CEO.
Lead and project manage company-wide strategic initiatives; bring together cross-functional stakeholders and drive decisions and action.
Develop and document internal processes for communications, operations, and other organizational needs.
Work closely with the Executive Assistant to the CEO to ensure appropriate management of the CEO's calendar, prioritizing tasks and meetings in alignment with organizational goals.
Serve as a key liaison between the CEO, the Executive Leadership Team, and external partners, adapting your communication style to build trust and accelerate decision-making.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor's degree required; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.
Strong financial acumen: demonstrated ability to interpret P&L statements, headcount plans, and translate financial data into clear executive recommendations.
Proven track record managing complex, cross-functional projects or programs end-to-end, with expertise in establishing systems to track progress and accountability.
Strong familiarity with AI-enabled tools and a willingness to champion AI adoption across the organization.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
Strong analytical capabilities: comfortable building analyses, interpreting data trends, and presenting actionable recommendations.
Demonstrated commitment to honesty, ethical conduct, and maintaining the highest levels of confidentiality.
Passion for OpenGov's mission of powering more effective and accountable government.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience in investment banking, private equity, venture capital, top-tier management consulting, Vertical Software, or as a Chief of Staff to a senior executive in a high-growth technology company.
Deep understanding of SaaS business models, with experience supporting financial planning or investor-facing processes.
Experience supporting a CEO or C-suite executive
Deep expertise in operational best practices and goal-setting frameworks (e.g., OKRs) that drive accountability and measurable outcomes.
Familiarity with GovTech or the public sector software market.

Compensation

Why OpenGov?

A Mission That Matters.

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.

A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.

Benefits That Work For You

A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

Through strategic relationship management and effective communication, the Director strengthens CIA's visibility, credibility, and impact among institutional funders and community partners.

Nature creates highly adaptable and efficient biological systems. The goal of the Biological Design Center (BDC) at Boston University is to unlock these design principles and reengineer them for applications in human health and the environment. To achieve this goal, the BDC brings together disparate research areas — including biology, engineering, physics, chemistry, and medicine — to create disruptive ideas and biomedical technologies, drawing in scientists from industry and academia to tinker, invent, and discover under the Center's auspices.

The Center is home to 21 core faculty and more than 150 researchers and trainees, spanning departments of engineering, sciences, computing, and medicine, and occupying three floors of the Rajen Kilachand Center for Integrated Life Sciences & Engineering. The BDC's deeply collaborative investigators advance cutting-edge research through federal, foundation, and industry support, and anchor two field-defining graduate training programs: the NIH T32 in Synthetic Biology and Biotechnology (SB2) and the NSF NRT in Biological Feedback Control.

The Executive Director leads the day-to-day operation of the BDC — driving the strategic, communications, and operational aspects of the Center's activities and programs, both facilitating the Center's growth and promoting its science on the global platform.

Overseeing the Center's Operations and Shared Research Infrastructure: The BDC's operations include purchasing and managing shared equipment, planning equipment maintenance and selective upgrades, overseeing the Center's facilities and resources, interfacing with other University offices and groups, implementing standard operating procedures, and maintaining a safe and positive environment at the Center.
Supporting the Center's Scientific and Training Programs: the BDC is home to a number of prestigious scientific training programs — including the NIH T32 SB2 program and the NSF NRT in Biological Feedback Control — for which seminars, workshops, training and professional development opportunities, symposia, and requests for applications, among other things, will need to be managed. The Executive Director also organizes the Center's annual symposium and seminar series and, where necessary, develops and implements new objectives and opportunities for training within the Center.
Managing the Center's Public Relations, Communications, and Marketing: this includes the Center's social media communications, website content, marketing and public relations programs and communications, and where necessary, interfacing with University Marketing & Communications offices.

Supervising the Center's Administrative Staff: this includes regular meetings, creating constructive, efficient and positive workplace practices, and delegation of the Center's administrative tasks.
Coordinating and Writing Multi-PI/Institution Grants: this involves supporting multi-PI and multi-institution grant efforts that advance the scientific goals of the BDC, including identifying faculty and institutions, and coordinating, writing, and submitting grant proposals to funding agencies.

Strong communication skills, with demonstrated ability to convey scientific and organizational information effectively.

CRIL History and Independent Living Philosophy

Community Resources for Independent Living (CRIL) was organized in 1979. CRIL’s main office is located in Hayward with branch offices in Fremont and Livermore. This sparked the independent living (IL) revolution that changed national law. Independent Living (IL) is a philosophy grounded in the principle that people with disabilities are the experts on their own lives. It champions the right of people with disabilities to make personal decisions, direct their own services, participate fully in community life, and empowers people to live as independently as they choose.

Reporting to the Vice President for Institutional Advancement, the Director is responsible for leading the College's institutional fundraising efforts, securing philanthropic and public funding that advances CIA's mission, strategic priorities, academic programs, student success initiatives, capital projects, and long-term sustainability.

The Director serves as the College's primary lead for foundation, corporate, and government relations, developing and implementing comprehensive strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward institutional funders. This position manages a portfolio of foundation, corporate, and public funding prospects while building meaningful relationships that generate significant philanthropic support for the institution. The Director develops compelling proposals, funding requests, and stewardship reports that communicate the impact of CIA's programs and priorities to external partners.

The Director is responsible for all aspects of grant development and administration, including identifying funding opportunities, preparing proposals and reports, ensuring compliance with funding requirements, and tracking institutional giving activity. Working collaboratively with faculty, academic leadership, and administrative departments, the Director helps translate institutional priorities into fundable initiatives and aligns funding opportunities with the College's strategic goals. This role also partners closely with the Business Office and project leaders to develop budgets, measure outcomes, and ensure responsible stewardship of grant-funded resources.

In addition, the Director serves as a key representative of CIA to foundations, corporations, government agencies, community organizations, and other external stakeholders. The position works collaboratively with legislative and advocacy partners to monitor public funding opportunities and supports efforts to secure government funding aligned with institutional priorities. Through strategic relationship management and effective communication, the Director strengthens CIA's visibility, credibility, and impact among institutional funders and community partners.

The successful candidate will be a highly skilled relationship builder, strategic thinker, and persuasive communicator with a demonstrated ability to secure institutional support and manage complex projects. They will bring a collaborative approach, exceptional writing skills, and a passion for advancing the mission of art and design education through philanthropy and partnership.

Qualifications

The successful candidate will possess a bachelor's degree in communications, nonprofit management, business, public administration, higher education, or a related field. A master's degree or other advanced degree is preferred.

Candidates should have three to five years of progressively responsible experience in fundraising, institutional giving, grant development, foundation relations, corporate relations, nonprofit advancement, or a related field. Demonstrated success securing grants or philanthropic support from foundations, corporations, government agencies, or other institutional funders is required.

Preference will be given to candidates with experience in higher education or nonprofit organizations, grant administration, donor database systems such as Raiser's Edge, and managing multiple concurrent funding opportunities and stakeholder relationships.

The successful candidate will demonstrate exceptional written and verbal communication skills, strong project management abilities, sound judgment, and the ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, administrators, trustees, donors, and community partners. Knowledge of fundraising ethics and best practices is essential.

Compensation

This is a full-time, exempt position. Compensation is commensurate with experience and qualifications. CIA offers a comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, holidays, health and dental insurance, retirement contributions, tuition remission, and more.

Review of applicants will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled.

Equal Opportunity Statement

CIA is committed to increasing diversity in our community and actively recruits individuals from all backgrounds. Additionally, CIA complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and provides equal opportunity in all educational programs and activities, admission of students and conditions of employment for all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, sex, religion, age, disability, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, gender identity, or national origin.

About Cia

CIA is also a great place to work, and manifesting a positive culture and sense of belonging is a big part of who we are. We work hard and are proud of our employees' collective contribution to our mission, but we also play hard and like to have fun. We challenge and support one another, integrate our institutional values in our work in a meaningful way, celebrate our successes, embrace learning and continuous improvement in all that we do, and are driven by our students' success and the creative environment that inspires us every day.

CIA is one of the nation's leading accredited independent colleges of art and design. Since 1882, the college has been an educational and cultural cornerstone in Cleveland, Ohio, producing graduates competitive as studio artists, designers, photographers, contemporary craftspeople, and educators. With approximately 600 students, CIA offers a personal educational experience with the benefits of a larger institution. CIA students can choose from 13 majors in fine and applied art, each leading to a Bachelor of Fine Arts. Students live and work in Cleveland's University Circle, one of the country's most unique cultural centers.

The mission of CIA is to cultivate creative leaders who inspire people, strengthen communities, and contribute to a thriving and sustainable economy through an innovative education in art and design. For more information, visit CIA's website.

Nature creates highly adaptable and efficient biological systems. The goal of the Biological Design Center (BDC) at Boston University is to unlock these design principles and reengineer them for applications in human health and the environment. To achieve this goal, the BDC brings together disparate research areas — including biology, engineering, physics, chemistry, and medicine — to create disruptive ideas and biomedical technologies, drawing in scientists from industry and academia to tinker, invent, and discover under the Center's auspices.

The Center is home to 21 core faculty and more than 150 researchers and trainees, spanning departments of engineering, sciences, computing, and medicine, and occupying three floors of the Rajen Kilachand Center for Integrated Life Sciences & Engineering. The BDC's deeply collaborative investigators advance cutting-edge research through federal, foundation, and industry support, and anchor two field-defining graduate training programs: the NIH T32 in Synthetic Biology and Biotechnology (SB2) and the NSF NRT in Biological Feedback Control.

The Executive Director leads the day-to-day operation of the BDC — driving the strategic, communications, and operational aspects of the Center's activities and programs, both facilitating the Center's growth and promoting its science on the global platform.

Specific Responsibilities Include

Overseeing the Center's Operations and Shared Research Infrastructure: The BDC's operations include purchasing and managing shared equipment, planning equipment maintenance and selective upgrades, overseeing the Center's facilities and resources, interfacing with other University offices and groups, implementing standard operating procedures, and maintaining a safe and positive environment at the Center.
Supporting the Center's Scientific and Training Programs: the BDC is home to a number of prestigious scientific training programs — including the NIH T32 SB2 program and the NSF NRT in Biological Feedback Control — for which seminars, workshops, training and professional development opportunities, symposia, and requests for applications, among other things, will need to be managed. The Executive Director also organizes the Center's annual symposium and seminar series and, where necessary, develops and implements new objectives and opportunities for training within the Center.
Managing the Center's Public Relations, Communications, and Marketing: this includes the Center's social media communications, website content, marketing and public relations programs and communications, and where necessary, interfacing with University Marketing & Communications offices.
Maintaining Oversight on and Managing the Center's Finances and Budget: this includes reporting on the Center's finances, assisting with annual reviews and reports, development and management of budgets and projections, and overseeing invoicing, disbursements, payroll, purchase orders, accounts receivables and/or payables.
Supervising the Center's Administrative Staff: this includes regular meetings, creating constructive, efficient and positive workplace practices, and delegation of the Center's administrative tasks.
Coordinating and Writing Multi-PI/Institution Grants: this involves supporting multi-PI and multi-institution grant efforts that advance the scientific goals of the BDC, including identifying faculty and institutions, and coordinating, writing, and submitting grant proposals to funding agencies.

Required Skills

Required Qualifications:

A PhD in biology, physical sciences, biomedical engineering, or a related field.

At least 3 years of related work experience post-graduation (such as in scientific administration, outreach, program management, or communications). Postdoctoral training is not required.

Demonstrated experience taking primary responsibility for a program, initiative, or operation from planning through execution — for example, running a training program, a seminar or symposium series, laboratory or core facility operations, or a comparable organizational unit.

Strong communication skills, with demonstrated ability to convey scientific and organizational information effectively.

Strong organizational skills and the ability to create structure and mechanisms around new programs and activities.

Experience contributing to grant proposals or comparable complex, multi-author scientific documents.

Ability to work with a diverse group of scientists, administrators, trainees, and staff members, and to navigate interpersonal relationships.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in an academic research center, institute, or core facility environment. Familiarity with shared research infrastructure, scientific equipment purchasing, or core facility operations. Experience coordinating multi-PI or multi-institutional grants, particularly training grants or center grants. Experience communicating science to both scientific and general audiences.

To Apply

Please submit a CV and a single PDF containing a brief cover letter and one writing sample of your own authorship — for example, a grant section, program or annual report, newsletter piece, or article written for a scientific or general audience (2–5 pages). Co-authored work is acceptable; please indicate which portions are yours.
